Arbor Hills Nature Preserve: A Quiet Triumph in Plano, Texas

📍 Location: 6701 W Parker Rd, Plano, TX 75093

🕒 Hours: Open daily, 5:00 AM – 11:00 PM

🐾 Dog-Friendly | 🚲 Bike Trails | 🌳 Wildlife Viewing | 🧺 Picnic Areas
⭐ Rated 4.6/5 on TripAdvisor and Yelp

Nestled in the heart of Plano, Texas, Arbor Hills Nature Preserve is a 200-acre sanctuary where the wild and the weary meet. Here, the trails—both paved and earthen—wind through prairies, woodlands, and creeks, offering a rare communion with nature just minutes from the city’s pulse.

The preserve welcomes hikers, joggers, mountain bikers, and families alike. Dog-friendly paths, shaded loops, and scenic overlooks make it a favorite for locals and travelers seeking a peaceful retreat. The playground and picnic pavilions near the entrance hum with laughter and quiet joy. Wildlife sightings—hawks, deer, armadillos—are not uncommon, and the air carries the scent of cedar and sun-warmed stone.

On weekends, the preserve can be crowded. Arrive early to find parking and solitude. The 2.7-mile mountain bike trail, maintained by DORBA, offers quick drops and banked turns for beginners and seasoned riders. The main loop trail, partially shaded, is ideal for walking meditation or a brisk jog.

In the evening, the light softens. Shadows stretch across the prairie. The world exhales.

Arbor Hills is not just a park. It is a place to remember that silence is not empty—it is full of meaning.

Context: Family nature walk on a Sunday

Pros:
Protected land where you can encounter Texas ecosystems on a variety of trails
Generally well-maintained (by DFW standards)
Bathrooms, drinking fountains, dog drinking fountains, maps are scattered about the trail system
The unpaved trails are less crowded than the paved - if you desire more nature, less people

Cons:
On Sunday morning at 11 am, we took one of the last two parking spots... be aware of peak times
Although generally well maintained, there are built environments on the trail that seem to be neglected, which include the framed educational installations, and the unpaved trails in general.
Specific examples include: A 4 ft. metal sign post rusting on the side of the Opossum Trail near the restrooms, grill filled with build up of charcoal in the same area, trail erosion do to insufficient gravel application.

Caveat: This perspective is given in light of a lot of time in states that place a high priority on park standards due in part to the stake they have in the tourist dollars. Colorado, Michigan, Washington. Relative to other nature spots in the greater DFW area, this is quite nice.
Not too crowded, great place for a casual walk. Dog friendly, too.

This is the most beautiful place in DFW. Lovely, assessible, well kept. I have enjoyed walking in every season. My big kids loved the play ground. The whole place is dog friendly. Feels really safe. Paved ways and dirt trails

Arbor Hills Nature Preserve in Plano, Texas is a true hidden gem and one of the best outdoor spaces in North Texas. The preserve offers a perfect mix of natural beauty and well-maintained trails, making it ideal for hikers, runners, families, and anyone looking to unwind outdoors.

The paved and unpaved trails are clearly marked and suitable for all fitness levels, whether you want a leisurely walk or a more challenging hike through the rolling hills. The scenery is beautiful year-round, with wildflowers in the spring, shaded paths in the summer, colorful foliage in the fall, and peaceful open views in the winter. The overlook tower provides a great view of the surrounding landscape and is well worth the short climb.

Arbor Hills is also very clean and well cared for, with helpful signage, restrooms near the entrance, and plenty of parking. It’s dog-friendly, family-friendly, and a great place for photography, picnics, or simply getting some fresh air.

Overall, Arbor Hills Nature Preserve is a wonderful escape from city life without leaving town. Whether you’re looking for exercise, relaxation, or a scenic spot to explore nature, this preserve is absolutely worth a visit.

Arbor Hills Nature Preserve is a true gem in Plano! The trails are beautifully maintained and offer a perfect mix of paved paths and natural dirt trails, so you can go for a casual walk, a run, or even some light hiking. The scenery changes throughout the park – open fields, wooded areas, and little streams – making every visit feel refreshing.

The lookout tower is a must-visit spot with great views of the city, especially at sunset. There are also plenty of shaded areas and benches to take a break, and the park feels safe and family-friendly.

Whether you’re walking your dog, biking, exercising, or just wanting some quiet time in nature, Arbor Hills has it all. It’s the perfect escape without leaving the city. 🌳✨

I visited Arbor Hills today. I used to frequent this area just to spend time in nature and enjoy my walk. I haven’t been to this area in a while until today because I moved out of the area. But today was a special day because I decided to come back and visit this beautiful nature preserve.

Indeed, Arbor Hills is a nature preserve. As you’re walking this season, you will notice the beautiful grassy plains swaying in the wind. There are an abundant of trails that you can take to explore different areas of the preserve. It is a great place to casually ride your bike and is also a popular destination for photography.

The nature preserve also has a well equipped playground for children to play and bathrooms for men and women and a family bathroom. There is also a picnic area that you can reserve to have gatherings.

Arbor Hills is a great place to walk your dog as they provide poop bags along the main path.

After finishing your walks and explorations, treat yourself to some ice cream from the ice cream truck that usually is parked near the restrooms in the afternoons, ready to happily serve customers.
